ordered_diagnoses: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas

s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva with a gradual increase in number over time
salient_findings: Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age and gradually increased
Family history of similar facial papules
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules are present on the face and vulva
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age
Lesions gradually increased to approximately 60
Patient has a medical history of meningioma
Family history is notable for a daughter with similar facial papules
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
Histopathology showed buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma was focally evident
Whole-exome sequencing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene

shortlist: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas

shortlist.label: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple basaloid skin lesions and a history of meningioma, consistent with this syndrome

shortlist.label: SUFU-related multiple basal cell carcinomas
shortlist.why_kept: Whole-exome sequencing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, which is associated with this condition

shortlist.label: Gorlin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome, with multiple basal cell carcinomas and a possible association with meningioma

shortlist.label: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology showed infundibulocystic lesions, which are characteristic of this condition

shortlist.label: Generalized basaloid follicular hamartoma syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple skin-colored papules with basaloid features, consistent with this syndrome

raw.rationale: The presence of a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, as revealed by whole-exome sequencing, strongly supports this diagnosis, especially given the clinical presentation of multiple basal cell carcinomas without other characteristic features of Gorlin syndrome such as palmar or plantar pits or jaw cysts.

rejected.label: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
rejected.why: Also known as Gorlin syndrome, this condition typically includes a broader range of features such as palmar or plantar pits, jaw cysts, and a higher incidence of other tumors, which are not all present in this case.

rejected.label: Gorlin syndrome
rejected.why: Similar to nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome, Gorlin syndrome encompasses a wider spectrum of manifestations not fully aligned with the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas
rejected.why: While this condition involves multiple basal cell carcinomas, the specific genetic mutation in the SUFU gene points more directly to SUFU-related multiple basal cell carcinomas.

rejected.label: Generalized basaloid follicular hamartoma syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves a different set of clinical and histological features, not matching the specific findings of basal cell carcinomas and the identified SUFU gene mutation in this patient.
